result: The ocean breathed in jagged rhythms, slamming its strong fists against the basalt cliffs. Rain didn't fall; it was driven sideways, a curtain of gray needles sewing the sky to the churning sea. Inside the lighthouse, the lens rotated with a hum so deep it vibrated in the teeth, a mechanical heartbeat keeping time against the chaos outside. A single ember glowed in the fireplace, casting long, dancing shadows that mimicked the frantic waves. Here, in this stone throat of the coast, there was only the ritual of light. The keeper wasn't a person anymore, just a memory of salt and oil, a ghost woven into the mortar, watching the beam slice through the dark. Every sweep was a promise, every rotation a reminder that even when the world drowns in thunder, the edge remains defined. The storm would eventually exhaust itself, sputtering into drizzle, and the sun would return to bleach the waves into indifferent glass. But for now, the light turned, unblinking, holding back the night with a silent, steady gaze that knew no fear, duty. The ocean roared its ancient anger, but the beam held, a golden needle threading the needle of darkness. The walls echoed with the whispers of a thousand previous storms, voices trapped within the flint and mortar, waiting for the door to creak open. Dust motes danced in the beam's aftermath, tiny survivors floating in the wake of the giant light, oblivious to the crushing depths below, standing vigil forevermore. The beam swept on.
